Subject: Logging & redaction controls - post-demo follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key items on logging and sensitive-data redaction so your security team has a clear picture of how Redwood handles request/response logs and header data. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps.

Recap (what we showed):
- Request/response logging: by default we capture request metadata and model responses for observability, error debugging, and quality monitoring.
- Redaction controls: customers can configure automatic masking rules for PII patterns (SSNs, credit card numbers, email addresses), plus selective redaction for request/response bodies and specific headers.
- Trace IDs & headers: trace IDs are stored as part of request metadata to correlate traces; we can mask or truncate trace IDs on a per-route basis if you need them omitted from persisted logs.
- Retention & residency: logs retention is configurable per-account (default 30 days); for regulated customers we support shorter/longer retention windows and can store logs in specific regions.

Questions / open items you flagged:
1) You want confirmation that we can redact: card PANs, SSNs, account numbers, and any custom regex patterns you provide.
2) Whether headers like Authorization or internal trace IDs are persisted in full or can be dropped/masked.
3) How long different log types are retained and whether we can provide an export for audits.

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a short engineering doc that outlines the redaction configuration and an example redaction YAML. Please review: redwood-logging-controls.pdf and redaction-config-example.yaml.
- Priya / Alex: can you share the specific regex patterns or examples of PII you want redacted? If you prefer, we can sign an NDA and your security team can upload a sample payload to our secure intake.
- I’ll loop in our infra lead (Dev) to confirm the technical options for masking trace IDs and header redaction options.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week with Priya and your security team. Proposed windows: Tue/Wed morning PST.

Thanks -
Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
redwoodinference.com

Thanks Marissa - helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Main ask: we need assurance that card PANs and full account numbers are never persisted in plaintext logs. Masking/pseudonymization is required.
- For trace IDs: we correlate traces across our services; we don't need full trace IDs in persisted logs for long-term storage, but we do need a deterministic hash so we can map back during short-term troubleshooting. Is deterministic truncation/hashing supported?
- Retention: our compliance team requires non-production logs retained for a maximum of 90 days, and production request/response logs retained for a maximum of 180 days. Is per-environment retention configurable?

We can get you sample payloads next week - we'll sanitize examples but want to ensure the redaction rules will catch our patterns. Also please confirm whether headers like X-Correlation-ID and Authorization are captured and how they can be excluded.

Alex -

Great questions. Quick answers below and then some implementation notes.

1) Card PANs / account numbers: we support schema-based and regex-based redaction. Out-of-the-box we mask common PAN patterns and account numbers. For your specific formats you can upload custom regex rules or a redaction whitelist/blacklist. Masking is irreversible in stored logs unless you request a controlled unmasking via a documented support flow (requires authorization).

2) Deterministic hashing for trace IDs: yes - we can persist a salted hash of the trace ID (SHA256 with per-account salt) so you can correlate without storing the raw ID. We can also configure time-limited plaintext retention (e.g., keep full trace ID for 7 days then replace with hash).

3) Retention per environment: configurable. We support per-environment retention policies (non-prod vs prod). We can set non-prod=90 days and prod=180 days as you requested. We also support on-demand exports for audit purposes.

4) Headers: Authorization is never persisted by default. X-Correlation-ID and similar headers are persisted in metadata by default but can be excluded or replaced with hashed values. We log a small set of headers for routing (Host, User-Agent) unless configured otherwise.

Implementation notes:
- I'll have Dev share the exact API for uploading custom redaction rules (the YAML format is in the attached example).
- For the salted-hash approach we'll need a per-account salt value (we generate by default; you can provide one if you want control).
- We can schedule the technical deep-dive - Dev and Ethan will join to scope the config and run through sample payloads.

Proposed next step: schedule a 30-min call next Tue (Jul 6) 10:00-10:30 PST. Is that good for your team?

Thanks -
Marissa
